newsitem.title: CHINA: China auto firm cuts price of VW Santana.
newsitem.headline: China auto firm cuts price of VW Santana.

text.p: The Shanghai General Automobile Sales Co, which sells Santana cars made by a joint venture with Germany's Volkswagen AG has slashed the price of the Santana 2000 model, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

The company has cut the retail price of the Santana 2000, which is made by Volkswagen and Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp, by as much as 16,800 yuan ($2,025) to 180,000 yuan, Xinhua quoted Xiao Guopu, general manager of auto sales, as saying.
The price cut was due to expanded production capacity at Shanghai Volkswagen, which is expected to produce 120,000 Santana 2000s this year, Xiao said.
"The company's real purpose is to get a bigger market share for the Santana line," Xinhua said, quoting industry analysts.
Shanghai Volkswagen sold 96,183 Santanas in the first five months of this year and the popular model was expected to account for half of total car sales in 1997, Xinhua said.
